advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the activation check use strict `-gt` (or sub-second/monotonic evidence) so a same-second start-vs-write tie is reported NOT in effect rather than in effect.
evidence: infra/scripts/docker-storage-cap.sh:139: `if [ -n "$written" ] && [ -n "$started" ] && [ "$started" -ge "$written" ]; then`
mtime_of prints `int(os.stat(...).st_mtime)` (truncated to whole seconds) at line 110, and docker_started_at reads /proc/<pid> mtime the same way — both second-granular

Comment at line 127-128 states the check 'FAILS CLOSED: anything undeterminable is reported as NOT in effect' but a same-second start-vs-write tie is reported as IN effect, contradicting that guarantee

The install path itself writes daemon.json (mv at line 330) then immediately calls report_activation_state; on a manual operator restart scheduled 'in a quiet window' the restart and a concurrent re-run could land in the same second
advisory.finding: The activation oracle compares process start mtime to daemon.json mtime with `-ge`, and both mtimes have 1-second resolution; a daemon that started (reading the OLD config) in the same second the new daemon.json is written satisfies `started -ge written` and is reported 'IS in effect' when the new policy is NOT actually loaded — a false-positive activation claim the whole check exists to prevent.
scenarios: Operator restarts docker and re-runs --install within the same second; script reports the cap IS in effect while the daemon may have read the prior file
Any automation that writes daemon.json and restarts docker in tight succession
advisory.suggested_fix: Use `[ "$started" -gt "$written" ]` so a tie fails closed, or compare with sub-second precision (e.g. st_mtime as float) so the daemon must demonstrably post-date the file write.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the two-independent-reads window in observability.sh §2f (du at :365 vs docker system df at :380) cannot cause a spurious rebar-docker-unaccounted-bytes page given the 2 GiB threshold + 2-of-3 hysteresis in monitoring_autodeploy.tf.
evidence: Shared mutable resource: bytes under "/var/lib/docker" — read twice as `du -sx --block-size=1 "$1"` (observability.sh:330 docker_du_bytes) and `docker system df --format '{{.Type}}|{{.Size}}'` (observability.sh: docker_ledger_bytes)
Read #1: docker_total_bytes="$(docker_du_bytes "$DOCKER_ROOT")" (observability.sh:365)
Read #2 (later, independent): docker_ledger="$(docker_ledger_bytes)" (observability.sh:380); difference: docker_unaccounted=$(( docker_total_bytes - docker_accounted_bytes )) (observability.sh:398)

Second+third executors: dockerd continuously writes overlay2/build cache, and autodeploy.sh runs `docker build`/`docker builder prune --keep-storage` on its own timer (autodeploy.sh:391-393) concurrently with the 5-minute observability timer (observability.sh:5)
Consumer / potential harm: docker_unaccounted_bytes feeds rebar-docker-unaccounted-bytes (monitoring_autodeploy.tf: comparison_operator GreaterThanThreshold, threshold 2147483648)

MITIGATION (guard) verified in code: monitoring_autodeploy.tf sets evaluation_periods=3, datapoints_to_alarm=2 and the 2 GiB threshold is documented as chosen ABOVE normal du/ledger divergence — a single transient interleaving skew is absorbed and does not page; a sustained >2 GiB residue is real accumulation, not an interleaving artifact
advisory.finding: observability.sh §2f computes docker_unaccounted_bytes as the difference of two independent, non-atomic reads of the live /var/lib/docker byte set (`du -sx` then `docker system df`), which dockerd and a concurrently-running autodeploy `docker build`/prune can change between the two reads; a transient skew is published as the residue metric.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the docker_unaccounted_bytes alarm remediation with the runbook: replace `docker system prune -a` with the runbook's dangling-only prune sequence, or explicitly protect :prev / live mcp tags.
evidence: diff (docker_unaccounted_bytes alarm_description): "REMEDIATION: stop the build path, then a daemon-level reclaim (`docker system prune -a` with the serving containers up, or a daemon restart scheduled per the runbook)"
runbook diff: "Never remove tagged images by hand: `compose-review-bot:prev` is the review-bot's rollback lifeline and the live `compose-mcp:<sha>` is the serving MCP release."
runbook diff remediation block uses only `docker builder prune -f` and `docker image prune -f` (dangling only), not `docker system prune -a`
autodeploy.sh:527-528 `docker image rm` WITHOUT -f so the daemon refuses while a container references an image — `system prune -a` bypasses that intent for reaped-but-retained rollback tags
advisory.finding: The `rebar-docker-unaccounted-bytes` alarm description recommends `docker system prune -a` as the daemon-level reclaim, but the same change's runbook explicitly forbids removing tagged images by hand because `compose-review-bot:prev` is the rollback lifeline and the live `compose-mcp:<sha>` is the serving release. `docker system prune -a` removes ALL images not referenced by a running container — including `:prev` and any reaped-but-retained per-release mcp tags — so an operator following the alarm's own first-line remediation destroys the rollback state the runbook and autodeploy.sh (mcp_reconcile_orphans, `docker image rm` WITHOUT -f) are built to preserve.
scenarios: Operator reacts to rebar-docker-unaccounted-bytes, runs the alarm's recommended `docker system prune -a`, and removes compose-review-bot:prev plus any retained mcp rollback tags whose containers are not currently running
advisory.suggested_fix: Change the alarm_description remediation to match the runbook (`docker builder prune -f` + `docker image prune -f`, then an operator-scheduled `systemctl restart docker`), and drop the `docker system prune -a` recommendation which removes tagged rollback images.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that renders with `--engine-version 25.0.3` against a daemon.json containing `{"builder":{"gc":{"defaultKeepStorage":"999"}}}` and asserts the merged gc has maxUsedSpace and NOT defaultKeepStorage (and the mirror case: legacy engine dropping a pre-existing maxUsedSpace).
evidence: infra/scripts/docker-storage-cap.sh:231-238 — comment: 'Assert exactly ONE of the two space keys and drop the other, so a box upgraded across the 25.0 boundary cannot end up carrying a stale key beside the live one' with `gc.pop("defaultKeepStorage", None)` / `gc.pop("maxUsedSpace", None)`

test_modern_engines_get_max_used_space and test_older_engines_get_default_keep_storage render into `daemon_json=tmp_path / "daemon.json"` (a nonexistent file => empty config), so the opposite key is never present to be dropped
test_the_merge_preserves_unrelated_daemon_configuration seeds `builder: {entitlements: ...}` but no `builder.gc.defaultKeepStorage`, so the pop path is still not exercised

ABSENCE: no test in tests/scripts/test_docker_storage_cap.py seeds a stale gc space key; searched for defaultKeepStorage/maxUsedSpace occurrences (lines 208,222,223,231,243,275) — all assert presence/absence in freshly-rendered configs, none assert removal of a pre-existing opposite key
advisory.finding: The stale-key drop on an engine-boundary upgrade (docker-storage-cap.sh lines 235/238: `gc.pop("defaultKeepStorage", None)` for modern, `gc.pop("maxUsedSpace", None)` for legacy) is untested: no test feeds a daemon.json that ALREADY carries the opposite space key, so the .pop() calls never actually remove anything under test and would still pass if deleted.
scenarios: A host upgraded from Engine 24.x to 25.x whose daemon.json already carries `builder.gc.defaultKeepStorage`; the modern render must drop it so the daemon does not carry a stale key beside maxUsedSpace
advisory.suggested_fix:
def test_upgrading_across_the_25_boundary_drops_the_stale_space_key(tmp_path):
    daemon_json = tmp_path / "daemon.json"
    daemon_json.write_text(json.dumps({"builder": {"gc": {"defaultKeepStorage": "999"}}}))
    result = _run(tmp_path, ["--print-json", "--engine-version", "25.0.3"], daemon_json=daemon_json)
    gc = _builder_gc(result.stdout)
    assert gc["maxUsedSpace"] == str(5 * 1024**3)
    assert "defaultKeepStorage" not in gc
# plus the mirror: seed maxUsedSpace, render --engine-version 24.0.7, assert it is dropped.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify `docker builder prune --keep-storage` accepts a bare byte integer on the engine version(s) this host runs, and handle the deprecated/renamed flag on Engine >= 25.0.
evidence: autodeploy.sh:145 `BUILD_CACHE_KEEP="${BUILD_CACHE_KEEP:-${DOCKER_BUILDKIT_CACHE_BYTES:-}}"` where DOCKER_BUILDKIT_CACHE_BYTES defaults to 5368709120 (a bare byte count)
docker-storage-cap.sh:264 `--print-env` emits `DOCKER_BUILDKIT_CACHE_BYTES=%s` as a plain integer
autodeploy.sh:392 `docker builder prune -f --keep-storage "$BUILD_CACHE_KEEP"` — prior value was the unit-suffixed `5GB` per the removed comment
ABSENCE: no test in the diff exercises `docker builder prune --keep-storage` accepting a bare integer against the engine versions this box may run
dropped.finding: `BUILD_CACHE_KEEP` now passes a bare byte integer (e.g. 5368709120) to `docker builder prune -f --keep-storage`, replacing the previous unit-suffixed literal `5GB`. `--keep-storage` acceptance of a bare integer (and the flag name itself) is docker-version-dependent — newer engines deprecated/renamed `--keep-storage` toward reserved-space flags — so on an engine that rejects a bare byte value the capped prune fails (non-fatal) and the on-demand BuildKit reclaim silently stops working while the log only says 'builder prune failed'.
scenarios: Docker engine where `--keep-storage` rejects a bare integer or the flag is renamed: the capped builder prune fails on every deploy, quietly reducing the BuildKit reclaim to only the emergency uncapped path
